subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — GPU sizing, throughput & unit economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Porter <jenna@acme-ai.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — GPU sizing, throughput & unit economics

Hi Jenna / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + requested follow-ups from our discovery: 

What we heard from your side:
- Target models: mix of 13B/70B decoder models for chat + a smaller reranker/embedding flow.
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~150M tokens/month in Q2, scaling to ~750M–1B tokens/month in 6–12 months.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 400ms for chat (user-facing).
- Throughput target: want to sustain ~200 tokens/sec aggregate now, with headroom to 500+ tokens/sec as usage grows.
- Budget ballpark: initial committed spend target $10k–$25k/month (open to commits to get reserved capacity).

Open questions for the pricing/engineering fit: 
1) GPU preference: do you have strict cloud GPU requirements? (A100-80GB vs H100) — this affects unit cost and whether we recommend quantized 70B variants.
2) Reserved capacity size: are you comfortable with a 3–6 GPU reserved pool initially, or do you want a larger 8+ GPU commit?
3) Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to get to ~$600–$800 / 1M tokens — can you confirm target $/1M tokens or a monthly invoice target?

Proposed next steps (from our side):
- I attached our pricing deck for Dedicated and an example committed-cost worksheet.
- Marcus / Aditya to confirm recommended GPU profile (H100 vs A100) and estimated throughput per GPU for the model mix.
- If agreeable, we'll run a short throughput test (we provide a lightweight harness) to validate tokens/sec and KV cache effectiveness.
- Draft a mutual action plan and target timeline for a pilot (we typically do a 2–4 week pilot on Dedicated).

Please reply with the GPU preference and confirm the target $/1M tokens (or a monthly spend target). Happy to jump on a 30m follow-up next week to align.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — GPU sizing, throughput & unit economics

Thanks Marissa, that recap is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- GPU preference: we prefer H100 if possible for the 70B models; we're OK with A100 for smaller models if that helps pricing.
- Reserved size: we'd like to start with 4 GPUs reserved (as a baseline) but want elasticity to burst to 8 when traffic spikes.
- Volumes: 150M tokens/month immediately, expect to ramp to ~900M by month 6 if the pilot performs well.
- Target unit economics: internally we're hoping for ~$600 / 1M tokens (that gives us margin at our price points). If you can show committed pricing in that neighborhood, we can push a PO.

Can Marcus/Aditya share estimated throughput per H100 for a mixed 13B/70B workload and any guidance on required CPU/memory for the serving nodes? Also, please send the throughput-test harness link.

Happy to do a follow-up Wed or Thu next week — Tom and I are available afternoons PT.

Best,
Jenna
Head of Product | Acme AI
jenna@acme-ai.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — GPU sizing, throughput & unit economics

Marissa / Aditya — quick technical POV to support the commercial ask below.

Short answer: H100 is the safer recommendation for mixed 13B/70B chat + reranking at scale if throughput is a primary driver. Expected ballpark throughput (single model, production codegen/attn kernels):
- H100 (80GB perf): ~1200–1500 tokens/sec per GPU for a well-optimized 13B chat model; ~300–450 tokens/sec per GPU for a 70B dense model (FP16 / q4 variants might increase throughput ~1.5x).
- A100 (80GB): ~800–1000 tokens/sec per GPU for 13B; ~200–300 tokens/sec per GPU for 70B.

For your mixed workload and desired aggregate 200–500 tokens/sec now -> we recommend starting with 4x H100s (reserved) to give headroom and better p95 latency. That configuration also maps well to a committed $/1M token target in the $500–$800 range depending on commit term (12mo vs monthly).

Notes on sizing:
- If you commit 4 H100s and use our autoscale burst to add 4 more for spikes, you'll meet both sustained throughput and burst needs.
- We should run a throughput test against your real prompt mix to validate the q4/quantized model performance; our test harness will simulate prefix cache hits and realistic sequence lengths.

I'll prep a quick spreadsheet with projected unit costs at different commit sizes (4, 8, 12 GPUs) and term lengths. Marissa, want me to attach that to the follow-up or is the pricing deck enough for now?

— Marcus

Thanks Marcus — that helps. Two quick follow-ups: 
1) For the throughput test, we'll want to include our typical prompt mix (avg length ~350 tokens, 10% > 1k). Can you confirm the harness supports variable seq lengths and KV caching behavior?
2) Regarding the committed pricing: our procurement prefers a 12-month commit. If you can show a price target at ~$600 / 1M tokens on a 12mo 4x-H100 commit, we should be able to get internal approval.

If you can share the projected cost spreadsheet, we'll validate against our finance model. Available for a 30m sync Wed 24 Feb 2026 2:30pm PT — does that work?

Best,
Tom
